page.layout: One page of text. Top: a block of italic verse across the full measure, continued from the previous page. Below a rule: a heading "III. GAL." and a French poem in roman with a large initial. Below that: a heading "LAT." and a Latin poem, with the catchword "Humanæ" at the right below the last line.

p.i: Pulchris, amœnis, seu colores, Seu varij placeant odores. Hîc alba florent Lilia cum rosa. Hîc suauitates cernis amaraci, Thimique, Narcissiq; iunctas Purpureo viola decori. Sed quum rigentis frigora sæuiunt Bruma, caduci tum vigor occidit Floris, iucundi tunc colores, Tunc varij fugiunt odores.

main_text.head: III. GAL.
main_text.p: L'EAV va viste en s'escoulant, Plus viste le trait volant, Et plus viste encores passe Le vent, qui les nues chasse, Mais de la ioye mondaine La course est si tressoudaine, Qu'elle passe encor deuant L'eau, & le trait, & le vent.
main_text.head: LAT.
main_text.p: FERVENTE torrens fugerit impetu Flumen, pererrant ocyus æthera Magnum sagittæ, quin sagittæ Præcipiti superantur Austro: Sed tam rapaci prætereunt fuga

page.notes: The Narcissiq mark is printed as a q with a flourish; read as "Narcissiq;" with a doubtful mark. The first line "Pulchris" is a fragment continued from the previous page. The faint text in the right margin is show-through from the reverse side and is not transcribed. Stains at the lower left are not printed text. Printed spacing in "Hîc suauitates" and some other lines is irregular, and the transcription follows the letters.
